reason: The cited evidence shows that aging can form nanoscale precipitates and increase strength (E1, E2, E3), but it also consistently demonstrates a severe ductility trade-off (E1, E2) or relies on a different alloy system and mechanism (E3). The premise that controlled nanoprecipitation avoids excessive embrittlement is directly contradicted by the cited refractory HEA data, and the predicted 10–20% strength increase with marginal ductility loss is not supported by the cited passages.
premises: Aging can precipitate nanoscale second-phase particles in refractory HEAs
Fine, discontinuously distributed precipitates obstruct dislocations and enhance strength
Controlled precipitate morphology (nanoscale, discontinuous) avoids excessive embrittlement
Aging at moderate temperatures (500–700 °C) for short times can achieve such precipitates
A strength increase of 10–20% with marginal ductility loss is achievable
